For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. The implemented dependency runs through `neorv32_cpu.frontend.i32 -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_nxt.csr_addr -> neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_addr -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu.frontend.i32` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.
